Missing-value codes in the SRTR formats, by type

Source: R/missing-codes.R
missing_codes.Rd

SRTR formats record missing information in several ways, and the same code number means different things in different formats: code 4 is "Unknown" in one format, "N/A" in another and "Not tested" in a third. Many flag columns have no format at all, so the dictionary does not say which of their values mean missing. This dataset classifies both kinds of code, so that each can be handled by what it means.

Format

A list of two tibbles.

formats has one row per classified format code:

Format, Code, Meaning

The format code, as in dictionary_versions. A classification applies only to this exact meaning.

missing_type

The type, one of those listed in Details.

collapses_to

For "partial" codes, the part of the answer that is known. Empty otherwise.

note

Why the code was classified this way, where that is not plain from its meaning.

variables has one row per variable and raw value, for values that no format of the variable lists. Most are one-character flag columns with no format:

Variable

The variable name, in whichever file it appears.

Code

The raw value, as text. A blank is the empty string. A blank or text value listed for a variable the dictionary types as numeric cannot occur as stored; such rows are kept from the hand list, and their note says so.

missing_type

The type, as above. Never "none" or "partial".

source

Where the row comes from. "hand list" rows were carried over from the hand-written list that srtr_normalize_missing() used before this dataset existed. The SRTR dictionary does not document these values, and they have not yet been checked against SAF data.

note

Anything else worth knowing about the row.

Source

formats: meanings from the SRTR SAF data dictionary pages stored in dictionary_versions, classified by hand in data-raw/missing-codes/format_codes.csv. variables: data-raw/missing-codes/variable_codes.csv, which is not taken from the dictionary.

Details

The classification describes what a code means. It does not say what an analysis should do with it.

A code is listed when its meaning matches a broad screen (words such as "unknown", "not done", "N/A" or "pending"), when it is the SAS missing value ., or when it is a format's catch-all. Each listed code was then classified by hand from its meaning in the SRTR data dictionary. A code the screen picked up that turned out to be an ordinary value is kept, with type "none", so that it is known to have been looked at. Codes that are not listed did not match the screen.

The types are sRtr's own grouping of the dictionary's meanings, not an SRTR classification:

  • "unknown": the information is not known.

  • "not_applicable": the question does not apply to this person.

  • "not_done": the test or assessment was not done.

  • "pending": a result was awaited.

  • "cannot_disclose": the result is withheld.

  • "indeterminate": the test was done and gave no clear result.

  • "partial": part of the answer is known, such as "Yes, duration unknown". collapses_to names the part that is known.

  • "sas_missing": the SAS missing value. For numbers that is ., which a format labels "Missing"; for text it is a blank.

  • "none": an ordinary value.
